supporting_observations.claim: Nora Blake launched Remote Desktop from her help-desk workstation to FILE-NWD-01, and the server recorded a successful type-10 interactive logon for her from that workstation.
Nora Blake later launched Remote Desktop to DC-NWD-01, and the domain controller recorded a successful type-10 interactive logon for her from WS-NBLAKE-01.
The inventory says remote administration is only done from WS-SOKAFOR-01; the observed RDP connections from WS-NBLAKE-01 are inconsistent with that stated practice and warrant investigation.
Dropbox was launched by Nora Blake. The inventory says Dropbox and other unapproved file-sharing services are not approved, but these process records alone do not show that files were transferred.

At 14:19 UTC, Nora Blake launched KB5034441_update.exe from C:\Windows\Temp with a quiet argument; the supplied records do not establish its signature, origin, privilege level beyond the recorded medium integrity, or effects.
The records also show Chrome opening Outlook on the web and OneDrive starting in the background, both consistent with services listed as approved in the inventory.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied records do not include a domain account-creation event or account/group membership changes for ext.rwong.
The RDP records establish interactive logons, but the supplied server-side activity does not show what Nora did in those sessions beyond standard session startup.
The Dropbox records show process launch and a signed module load, not Dropbox network activity or file transfers.
The installer records do not include a hash, signature status, download or file-creation history, subsequent process activity, or execution outcome.
The proxy records expose connection and request metadata but do not establish the content of encrypted traffic.
claims_not_established: Whether ext.rwong was actually created, who created it, or whether it was added only to the Freelancers group.
Whether the RDP sessions or Dropbox launch were authorized exceptions or part of malicious activity.
Whether any files or credentials were accessed, copied, or exfiltrated during the observed activity.
Whether KB5034441_update.exe was legitimate, malicious, or successfully performed an update.
Whether Nora Blake's activity was connected to the reported account alert.
additional_evidence_needed: Domain controller security and directory audit events around 13:42 UTC, especially account creation, group membership changes, and the initiating subject and source host.
FILE-NWD-01 and DC-NWD-01 session activity for Nora's RDP logons, including process creation, file access, privilege use, and session termination.
Dropbox network and file-access telemetry, including any uploads or synchronization activity.
The installer file's hash, signature, origin, creation/download events, and subsequent execution or update results.
Confirmation from the help desk and IT administrator about whether the server RDP sessions, Dropbox use, and installer execution were authorized.
